::: {.why}
Columnar storage with predicate pushdown means a well-designed layout reads a fraction of the bytes, and the difference between a good and a bad partitioning is a factor you measured last night.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Explain predicate pushdown and column pruning, and demonstrate both with measured bytes read.
- Choose a partitioning scheme for your own store and defend it against the query pattern.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure the two mechanisms separately: read one column of one year from a partitioned dataset, then all columns of one year, then one column of all years. The three byte counts show pruning and pushdown independently, and having seen them you will stop guessing about layout.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Choose and implement a partitioning scheme, then check the failure mode: too many small partitions makes metadata dominate. Report the file count, the average file size, and the query time across three schemes, and pick from the measurements.
:::
:::
